page: Vultr voc-s-1c-8gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server provides 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 1 thread per core, ensuring dedicated CPU allocation without hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, and is bundled with 150 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is positioned in the top tier (top 10%) at 3373.08, and single-threaded compression tasks show strong results, with gzip compression at 31.57 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.38 GB/sec. However, due to the single-core limitation, multi-core benchmarks are weak or poor, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1930.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 2969.39. Memory bandwidth is average for large blocks at 40.43 GB/sec read and 36.8 GB/sec write, but weak for small cached blocks.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its strict single-threaded design, which limits its utility for parallelized workloads, software compilation, and multi-threaded database operations. This is reflected in the poor multi-core Geekbench compiling score of 2020.0 and weak Passmark database operations score of 1111.63. Qualitatively, the server offers high resource density for memory and storage relative to its single dedicated CPU core, making it a cost-efficient option for memory-intensive, single-threaded applications. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, small-scale LLM inference text generation, and workloads requiring dedicated CPU execution with a moderate memory footprint.
